1#main: The law of the firstborn after slaughter, and that one may not sell it nor slaughter it until a blemish befalls it. In it are 3 seifim. One does not flay a firstborn—meaning, to remove its hide whole through its legs.
2#main: If he slaughtered it and it was found a treifah, its hide with its flesh is forbidden in benefit and requires burial. (Therefore it is good to sell it to a gentile before slaughter (Hagahos Mordechai, chapter HaIshah, and so Beit Yosef in the name of an Ashkenazic responsum, and it is in a responsum of Maharil).)
3#main: The kohen must maintain it and raise it forever until a blemish befalls it; and he may sell it, even to an Israelite, even though it is unblemished; and the buyer observes upon it the sanctity of the firstborn. In what case is this said? When the buyer acquires it for his need; but it is forbidden to make commerce with it—meaning, to buy it in order to profit. And if he bought it for his need and did not need it, he may return and sell it.
